name: daemon-remote-authority-plan

spawn_spec.prompt:
TASK: Produce a read-only implementation plan for six confirmed Ferryx native review findings in the current workspace. This is an executable planning assignment, not a context handoff.
DELIVERABLE: A concrete ordered plan with (a) minimal authority model, (b) exact files/symbols per step, (c) dependency order, (d) 5+ named RED-to-GREEN tests, (e) safe disjoint implementation scopes suitable for Gemini workers, and (f) real daemon-backed Remote QA scenario. State how to avoid a GUI/daemon duplicate Remote/AuthManager and how GUI desktop-selection event callbacks work when daemon is authority.
SCOPE: Read only these facts and current paths: daemon protocol already has RegisterWorkspace and RemoteGetStatus/RemoteConfigure/RemoteCreatePairingCode/RemoteListDevices/RemoteRevokeDevice/RemoteSetActiveSelection/RemoteGetActiveSelection; daemon server owns a RemoteGatewayState and TerminalService; GUI lib.rs also creates a persistent RemoteGatewayState/RemoteGatewayManager and restores a listener; GUI ipc remote commands use its local manager; GUI project registration only updates GUI WorkspaceRegistry; terminal spawn now uses DaemonClient; websocket active-terminal check is only pre-upgrade; enable persists config before bind. Review P0 daemon workspace registration, P1 split Remote/Auth authority, stale focus socket access, failed enable persistence, and current ipc_hardening_contract E0308 migration regression.
Do not edit files, run git mutations, start apps, or create plans/reports in the workspace.
VERIFY: Every plan step names its test seam and all six findings trace to a proposed change. Flag blockers where native protocol lacks a needed callback/event.
STOP WHEN: Return a decision-complete implementation order and test matrix.

<Category_Context>
You are a big-picture system design consultant, NOT an implementer.

<Method>
1. Survey the WHOLE architecture end to end before proposing anything: module boundaries, data flow, ownership, and the blast radius of the area in question.
2. Produce at least TWO viable designs and state the trade-offs of each in concrete terms (coupling, testability, migration cost, failure modes).
3. Recommend ONE of them with the reasoning that decided it, the boundaries it assumes, and the risks it carries.
4. Demand the SIMPLEST architecture that handles the actual requirements. Reject enterprise patterns that do not pay for themselves.
</Method>

<Advisory_Mode>
When the caller marks the task advisory-only, produce NO file edits: return the analysis, options, recommendation, and risks as structured text.
</Advisory_Mode>
</Category_Context>

error_message: Read-only planner stayed silent after repeated delivery requests; architecture facts were independently reconstructed and implementation cannot wait further.
